parent.description: Parent board id, null for root

relatedBoards.description: Board ids this room is related to. Purely declarative: it tells the renderer which rooms may share colour and wire treatment, so a relation is visible at a glance instead of remembered. See docs/02 Relation colour.

node.$strictness: additionalProperties:false is deliberate and matches $defs/edge. Without it a typo like "cdw" instead of "cwd" validates clean and the node silently fails to resolve at runtime — the exact class of bug this schema exists to catch. Every field a node may carry is declared below; the allOf branch below only adds `required` (conditionally, via its provisional gate), never new properties, so it does not interact with this.

designator.description: U4, J2, D7 — auto-assigned per room

footprint.description: In tiles. Defaults per kind if omitted. Scalable from the node editor, by dragging the corner handle in Edit Board mode, or with Shift+arrows. The interactive cap is per kind — see maxFootprintFor() in packages/shared/types.ts — because a group.zone is a bracket drawn around a cluster and is meant to span a room, while a component is an object you pick out at a glance.

provisional.description: Unpopulated footprint — a TODO on the board

codexRef.description: Path within codex/ describing this thing

prelaunch.description: Named update steps to run before the session starts. Ids only — the shell text lives in packages/shared/prime-steps.ts, because docs/07 forbids executable strings in board JSON. Omit for the safe default; [] to prime nothing.

addDirs.description: Directories outside cwd this agent may read and write, passed as claude --add-dir. How one agent oversees repos scattered across the disk without moving them.

readOnLaunch.description: Documents the session reads first, repo-relative, in order. Omit to derive from CLAUDE.md + persona + codexRef; [] to open with no reading.

briefing.description: When the session briefing is sent. first = new conversations only; every = re-orient on resume too.

boardFile.description: Relative path to the child board JSON

versionPattern.description: Regex with one capture group for the version label

relation.description: A board id. On a group.zone, draws the zone outline in that board's signal colour, marking this cluster as related to that room. Colour only — no behaviour.

image.description: WALLPAPER. Path to any image on disk, stretched to fill the whole footprint, dithered onto the room's six palette colours and drawn as the component's face. The source file is never copied or modified; the mosaic is cached in userData and regenerated when the file changes. If the file moves, the node renders broken like any other unresolved target.

logo.description: LOGO. A smaller image centred on the face, aspect ratio preserved, with its own bevel so it reads as a badge sitting on the wallpaper. Sized by logoBoxTiles() in packages/shared/types.ts — proportional to the footprint, always a whole number of tiles.

showDesignator.description: Print the reference designator (U4, J2) on the package. Turn it off for a node you want to read as a picture or a title alone.

showName.description: Print the name on a nameplate above the package. Turn it off for a node whose thumbnail or designator says enough.

showThumbnail.description: Draw the wallpaper (`image`). Off keeps the drawn package silhouette and leaves the image bound to the node. Independent of showLogo.

showLogo.description: Draw the logo badge (`logo`) centred on the face. Independent of showThumbnail, because the two are separately useful: a recognisable badge on a drawn package with no photograph behind it, or a photograph with no badge over it.

part.description: Which piece of board furniture this decor.part is. Each maps to a decor.* sprite in assets/sprites/manifest.json, cut from a real tilesheet cell.

pulseGlow.description: Animate the wallpaper as a wave of energy travelling outward from the node's centre. A palette shift along the room's own six-colour brightness ramp, not a translucent glow — see src/renderer/board/glow.ts. Costs one set of precomputed frames per image; off under reducedMotion.

textColor.description: Colour of this node's printed text. A palette token, never a hex string — signal/mask-dark/mask-light mean something different in every room, and a hex value can be off-palette.

textStroke.description: A 1px outline stamped around every glyph, in this token. Omit for none.

textPlate.description: Print the text on a plate: a filled box with a 1px border and its corner pixels omitted, sized to the text. Keeps a legend readable where the board is busy.

plateColor.description: The plate's fill. Defaults to the room's mask-dark.

plateBorder.description: The plate's border. Defaults to copper-dark.

textGlow.description: Pulse the text brighter and back along the room's own colour ramp. Off under reducedMotion.

frame.description: The copper that hangs off the edge of this node — pin legs, connector fingers, mounting tabs, a socket ring, a pad array. Drawn in a margin OUTSIDE the footprint, like the nameplate, so collision and routing are unaffected.

priority.description: How important this node is, shown as physical height: each level is two pixels of long shadow cast down and to the right. 0 is flat, 5 sits ten pixels proud. Deliberately thin — it is a hierarchy cue, not a skyline.

elevated.description: file.exe only: ask Windows to start this program as administrator. Opt in per node; a UAC prompt appears on every launch. SkynetOS itself never runs elevated — it asks Windows to start an elevated child. See docs/07-SECURITY.md.

rotation.description: decor.part and decor.image only: quarter-turn rotation, clockwise. Quarter turns only — any other angle would resample the pixels, which docs/02 Anti-mush forbids.

allOf.$comment:
A node must declare its target UNLESS it is provisional.

Every branch below says "a node of this kind points at something real, so name the thing" — a store.repo has a path, a link.url has a url, an agent.code has a cwd and a launch. That is prime directive 1 and it stays.

But `provisional: true` is the board saying, in the one word it has for it, that this node does not point at anything yet: it renders as an unpopulated footprint, a TODO printed on the board, which is a real PCB convention and the whole reason the flag exists. Demanding a target from a node that has openly declared it has none is a contradiction, and it had a cost: services/node-factory.ts creates every new node unbound and provisional by design, so the "+" palette could not add a link, a repo, a backdrop, a build or an agent at all. The edit was rejected before it reached the board.

So the requirement is conditional on the claim. Bind it and it must resolve; mark it a TODO and it must look like one.

A document is a document whether it lives on a disk or behind a URL. William's Word files are in OneDrive; the ones he has not synced have an https address and no path at all. Forcing `path` would mean either a second node kind for the same thing, or a node that renders broken forever. See requiredOneOf in packages/shared/node-fields.ts.

relation.description: A board id. Draws this trace's inner strand in that board's signal colour, so a wire that leads to another room carries that room's identity. Colour only — it changes nothing about routing or behaviour.
